segments.html:
The wizard, from the goal down to the checks

Seven levels. Read top to bottom: each one zooms into the boundaries of the one above. Dashed frames are boundaries; every arrow names what crosses and the shape it has.

L0 Goal: one codebase, three ways to run it

A person at a terminal, a headless workflow, or a parent process driving any agent over a socket. The parts inside the process never know which one is happening. Everything that leaves the machine is HTTPS.

L1 Surfaces: the import boundary

Four source roots. A surface imports another only through its public entries; instances cross the other way by injection. store imports no surface; tui and agent never meet. The compiler, an architecture suite, and a bundle audit enforce the same matrix.

EdgeBoundary crossedCarriesShape
cli → storesurfacethe store class, the UI accessor, programs, the control server@store, @store/types, @store/programs; @store/control by dynamic import from two runner files
cli → agentsurfaceone agent runrunAgent(config: ProgramRunConfig, session: WizardSession, { composed? })
cli → tuisurfacethe render entry and the console renderersstartTUI → TuiHandle { store, unmount, waitForSetup }; LoggingUI, HeadlessUI
tui → storesurfacewhat screens read and commitFlowStoreApi = Pick<FlowStore, 63 names>; Flow, FlowStep; flow keys as ScreenId
agent → storesurfacehow a run reports and what it readsWizardUI (44 methods + interactive); ProgramRunConfig; ask bridge, tools
store → any surfacesurfacenothingno import; instances arrive by setUI, new FlowStore(flow), hooks

Injection closes the loop the other way: cli installs StoreUI or LoggingUI with setUI, hands FlowStore to the TUI and the control server, and hands ControlHooks to the server.

L2 Objects: what attaches to what at runtime

One FlowStore per process, one RunStore per agent run. Every writer reaches the store through one contract; every reader subscribes to one store. The agent only ever sees WizardUI and its own session copy.

L3 Data: who owns which key

A key lives in exactly one place. The flow keeps what a later run must see; a run keeps what a later run must not. The wire gets a whitelist of the merge and never a secret.

EdgeBoundary crossedCarriesShape
flow → store.sessioninside storeeverything that outlives a runWizardSession map
run → store.sessioninside storethe active run's keysRUN_SESSION_KEYS (8) laid over the flow

never on the wireprocess → socketaccess token, API key, user record, answers, vaultcredentials reduce to a boolean; answers are recorded as ids and prompts only

The two artefact URLs (dashboard, notebook) moved to the flow after a real self-driving run showed run 2 wiping what run 1 created.

L4 Wire: the control API as the store on a socket

A route is a store question, a store setter, or one of four hooks for what the store cannot do. Screen-gated actions keep keyboard parity; named setters give a parent full store controls; a run request lays data fields over a program.

EdgeBoundary crossedCarriesShape
GET /statesocketthe store, readControlState; ?wait=&since= resolves on version > since
POST /actions/:idsocketa commit legal on the current screen{ params } → one setter; same setter the key handler calls
POST /store/:settersocketa commit whatever the screen{ params } → one of 25 CONTROL_SETTERS, each a STORE_BOUNDARY_MEMBERS name
POST /runssocket → hookone independent runRunStartBody: programId or skillId, installDir?, frameworkContext?, config? (7 data fields)
GET /runssocketthe ledgerRunRecord: runId, programId, skillId, installDir, status, error, timestamps, result = ControlState at run end
POST /credentials · /detect · /shutdownsocket → hookwhat the store cannot doControlHooks; 409 while running, 501 on the other surface
errorssocketevery bad input400 param/action/setter/program, 404 route, 409 in flight, 413 > 64 KB, 415 not JSON, 500 hook, 501 surface

L5 A run: what goes in, what comes out

Independent by construction. The agent receives a run config and a session copy, speaks only through WizardUI, and its RunStore is discarded by the next run. Composition (which run after which, with what context) lives above, in the cli or the parent.

EdgeBoundary crossedCarriesShape
config → agentstore → agentwhat to runProgramRunConfig from runConfigFor(config); functions in run never cross the socket, data fields may be overlaid
session → agentstore → agentas whom and whererun.session: a copy with installDir, merged frameworkContext, skillId

outcome → parentstore → sockethow it endedRunRecord.result = ControlState at run end; runPhase settles before the record does

L6 Enforcement: what fails if a boundary moves

The same rule is checked three ways so it cannot drift in one place: the compiler, tests that scan the source, and an audit of the built chunks. Under them, one Vitest project per surface and real socket-driven runs.

Deep dive with runtime scenarios, evidence, review findings, and decisions: the canvas "Wizard surface split: architecture report" in this channel. Source PRs: PostHog/wizard #1269 to #1283.
